title: Dynamic connection-slimming and latency containment for KV/stream dependencies
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Aim: implement a middleware-driven dynamic connection-slimming layer + containment windows across Redis/KV and Kafka clients to prevent single-backend tail behavior from violating tenant SLOs. The feature combines per-tenant SLO budgets, adaptive max-connections (conn-slimming), probabilistic request hedging, and a lightweight tiered-degradation policy (cache-first, stale-read, then skip). This ticket covers design, instrumentation, canary rollout, and initial chaos experiments. The approach targets three failure modes: connection/queue saturation, backend latency spikes, and cross-region fanout amplification.
acceptance_criteria: Conn-slimming middleware deployed behind feature flag in two services
Under synthetic backend latency spike (1000ms mean, 3s tail) overall tenant P99 latency increase < 1.5x and error rate stays within SLA budget
Circuit score and conn-slimming metrics (conn_limit, queued_reqs, shed_count) emitted to metrics and visible on dashboard
Canary in eu-west-1 at 5% traffic for 48h with automated rollback on SLO breach
Load test report (artifacts) demonstrating improvement in regional failover behavior and reduced blast radius
rollout_plan: 1) Merge behind feature-flag to runtime branch; 2) Canary 5% in eu-west-1 (48h) with active monitoring; 3) Ramp to 25% if no SLO regressions for 72h; 4) Enable cross-region hedging rules in a separate staged flag; 5) Full rollout after 1 week and post-rollout smoke tests. Rollback: flip flag and drain new conn limits. Runbook attached to incident playbook.
decisions: Use middleware approach in client library vs. modifying runtime kernel to maximize rollout speed
Per-tenant conn limits should be soft (probabilistic shedding) before hard rejects to reduce cascading failures
Circuit scoring will use a 60s sliding window combining error rate, queue depth, and 95th latency into a single heuristic score
Hedging window default = 50ms for regional fanout; made configurable per route
open_questions: Default per-tenant conn limit: 20 vs 50? need production histogram analysis
Should stale-read fallback be global (service-level) or per-route?
Integration with existing tenant-admission lane priorities - do we preempt lower-priority traffic?
What are safe defaults for kafka produce backpressure (acks, linger) when conn-slimming triggers?
implementation_notes: Add ConnSlimmer middleware to clients/common: track active_conns, inflight, queued, rejected counts
Expose control-plane API to adjust per-tenant parameters from Console and auto-scaler
Integrate circuit scorer into runtime routing to prefer region-fallback when score > threshold
Instrumentation: emit conn_limit, conn_in_use, queue_time_ms histogram, shed_count, circuit_score as tags by tenant and route
Graceful behavior: honor KV cache TTLs and prefer returning cached values before doing remote call
Include concurrency unit tests, bench harness for redis/kafka mocks, and end-to-end chaos test for regional failover
test_plan: Unit tests for middleware logic, synthetic bench with redis-mock and kafka-mock to validate conn limits under load, end-to-end canary with real kafka+redis in staging, chaos experiments injecting 500-3000ms latency and connection resets, and SLO regression tests using the existing SLO harness. Collect traces and compare baseline vs experiment for p50/p95/p99 and error budgets.
